name: Link and Pin (Link and Pin Apartments)
award: 2025 Federal 4% and noncompetitive state housing tax credits
headline: Lincoln Avenue Communities plans Link and Pin, about 150 new apartments (mostly studios and one-bedrooms) for households at 30% to 80% AMI on Fox Street in Globeville, near the 41st and Fox rail station. It won a 2025 federal 4% award from CHFA plus noncompetitive state credit and transit-oriented communities (TOC) credit, backed by City of Denver bonds.
why_it_matters: This bond deal is in Denver's pipeline right now. The issuance ordinance (up to $27M, including $19.4M of city bond cap) was filed on 2026-10-20 for committee on 2026-10-27 and council readings in November, and it names the bonds Series 2027A and 2027B.

status.label: Credits awarded; bond ordinance before Denver City Council; not closed
status.detail: Denver adopted the bond inducement on 2026-07-27. The issuance ordinance was introduced on 2026-10-20, with committee planned for 2026-10-27 and final reading for 2026-11-16. No financial closing, building permit or groundbreaking record was found.

next_step: Watch for Denver's Finance and Business Committee vote on Bill 26-1605 (2026-10-27) and the council readings on 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-16, then the bond closing.

key_numbers.meaning: 30 at 30% AMI, 68 at 60%, 14 at 70% and 38 at 80%. The mix is 72 studios, 50 one-bedroom, 14 two-bedroom and 14 three-bedroom units. Denver's records count 149 units.
About $28.3M over 10 years. CHFA also lists $700,000 of noncompetitive state credit and $195,000 of TOC credit.
Denver's ordinance would allow up to $27M in tax-exempt Series 2027A and taxable Series 2027B bonds, using up to $19.4M of city bond cap.
Lincoln Avenue applied to the Division of Housing in the February 2026 round. No award was found.

facts.value: CHFA prints 4159 Fox St, Denver 80216. Denver's bond records place the project at 4187 Fox Street in Globeville.
Family, new construction, in a QCT (not a DDA or SADDA); Section 8 column marked No
150 total, 150 low-income per CHFA; about 149 per Denver and the Division of Housing
Link and Pin Apartments LP, a Colorado limited partnership
District 9, per the inducement resolution (the October 2026 bill request says District 11)

In 2015 Denver rezoned 4143-4159 North Fox Street from light industrial (I-A, UO-2) to C-MS-8 (urban center main street, 8 stories), as part of a rezoning near the 41st and Fox station. Bill 15-0586 passed on 2015-09-28. Whether it covers the whole current site is inferred, not confirmed.

background.text: The name predates Lincoln Avenue. In CHFA's 2023 Round Two, Rainier Development applied for a 270-unit, all-affordable project called Link and Pin at 4149 Fox Street. It asked for $4,225,835 a year in 4% credit, $1.1M in state credit and $44M in CHFA bonds. Its letter of intent called the project Fox Street, at 4159 North Fox Street.
The 2023 Rainier application was not among the 10 developments CHFA awarded in 2023 Round Two.
Lincoln Avenue Communities applied to the Division of Housing for $2.5M for Link & Pin Apartments (149 units) in the February 2026 round.

Denver's Finance and Business Committee approved the inducement on 2026-07-14, and City Council adopted Resolution CR26-0998 on 2026-07-27. It is subject to a bond purchase commitment, City approvals and design approval, and a final bond ordinance. The cap award expires after one year unless extended.

The Department of Finance's 2026-10-16 bill request sets out the calendar: Finance and Business Committee on 2026-10-27, Mayor-Council on 2026-11-03, first reading on 2026-11-09 and second reading on 2026-11-16.
The 2027A/2027B series names suggest the bonds are expected to be issued in 2027 (inferred from the names only).

Planned second reading of the bond ordinance at City Council

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists 150 units, while Denver's bond records and the Division of Housing list 149 units.
CHFA gives the address as 4159 Fox St, while Denver's bond records place the project at 4187 Fox Street.
CHFA lists 68 units at 60% AMI, while Denver's October 2026 bill request lists 67. The July 2026 inducement request listed 30 units at 30%, 75 at 60% and 30 at 80% AMI.
CHFA lists the bonds at $17,400,000, while Denver's inducement and ordinance award up to $19,400,000 of city bond cap within up to $27,000,000 of total bonds.
The inducement resolution places the project in Council District 9, while the October 2026 bill request lists Council District 11.
